notes.title: Patch notes 0.2.13 - UI overhall
notes.content:
Whoa dudes, brace yourselves for some totally radical updates straight from the Untamed Dragons of Medieval Darkness otherwise known as yours truly, the Mech Monkey Devs!

[b]Demo Release Date Picked![/b]
Get ready to call in sick and totally clear your calendar on September 3rd. Demo is coming! This is in preparations for a totally gnarly October Next fest on steam.

[b]Totally Righteous UI Overhaul, Dude[/b]
The UI has been completely revamped in menus and gameplay… Now it’s way more metal and definitely more righteous to look at. All the screens are tuned to shred harder than ever before
[b]Dodge System Gets a Makeover[/b]
The dodge system has been converted to jam with the skill system
 Now you can bust out dodge moves that sync up with your skills and keep you shredding baddies in style.

[b]Match Over Screen Fixed[/b]
The match over screen was bogus before and didn’t show up right
 Now it pops up correctly every single time… no more glitches wrecking your vibe
Stay stoked, keep it metal, and we’ll see you at Next Fest... party on and stay medieval!
-Mech Monkey Devs

notes.title: Patch notes v0.2.12
notes.content:
Alright, warriors of rock and wielders of the wicked, this patch brings the heat. We’ve tuned up combat, and added style in all the nice spots... Let’s break it down.

Movement & Combat – Future so bright we gotta wear shades!

Dodge Roll added! Press Control + any direction to dive, roll, and not die.

Input system upgraded to prepare for full controller support. You can now throw hands with a gamepad, basic combat only so far!

Attack animations fixed, mostly... no more getting stuck like a confused statue mid-swing.

Blocking now shows proper shield animations. Look cool while surviving.

Certain weapon types now actually show their animations. Radical.

Hit reactions have a cooldown now. No more being flung into a flinch loop.

Skills: Power Up, Blacksmith Style

New Blacksmith Skill: Metalhead’s Mockery – An exclusive taunt. Draws heat, drops attitude.

Armor Mastery (Passive): Blacksmiths get a base armor bonus. Start strong, stay strong.

Firebolt (Mage): Now has a 1.5 sec cast time, costs more mana, and deals more damage. Putting points into it speeds up casting.

Gear – Look Good, Hit Hard

Ancient Mace of Lightning no longer spams the logs or looks janky. Zap responsibly.

Sunglasses are officially “face gear” now. Combine with helmets for custom creations.

New starter rock t-shirts featuring Ithule’s Second coolest band: Moodminder. Collect the whole set (eventually).

New gear line: ThunderChrome... For Templars and tanks who want their armor to hit as hard as their soundtrack.

Scene Fixes – Naughtwood Gets a Patch-Up

Tavern roof added over the crafting area. Less rain, more forging. Try jumping on it if you dare.

Mobs – Slightly Less Wild Now

Tiger cubs’ colliders fixed. No more phasing through reality.

Questing – A Little More Guidance, A Lot More Groove

Naughtwood outer-area quests now require level 2, except for the Mayor’s intro quest.

That's all we got now amigos.  Until next time, stay tuned. Same Bat time, same bat channel!
- Mech Monkey Devs

notes.title: Patch notes v 0.2.11
notes.content:
[h1]Medieval Darkness Patch v0.2.11 – The Quest for Quality Update[/h1]
Whoa, dudes. Version 0.2.11 just crash-landed like a flaming meteor of bug fixes and sweet, sweet polish. 
If you've been wandering around wondering why your NPCs were zoning out at the fountain or why you couldn’t sit down without spiritually detaching from your character... this one’s for you.
[b]Let’s kick things off with the UI[/b], because yeah, it got some serious love. Quest markers are finally showing up for everyone, not just the chosen few. 
The mission table won’t trap your soul anymore, and using the Build Menu won’t freeze you into a moving statue of shame. 
[b]Bulk sell? [/b]You better believe it works now. Sell all your junk in one glorious burst of coin-clinking freedom. 
[b]Also, the “go to task”[/b] markers got a size boost, and there's more of them. Now the townsfolk aren’t just yelling at you from across the void—you can actually find them. Even the Relic icon decided to match itself, onscreen and off. About time, right? Oh, and chat bubbles? Way easier to read. Say what you will, and actually have people read it.
[b]Monsters got a brain upgrade too.[/b] The lizard guys finally figured out players are more interesting than treasure chests. Their armor no longer floats mysteriously at a distance like some kind of cursed fashion show. 
And hey, Summoned Ironfist? He’s been hitting the gym. He’s tougher now, but don’t freak out this isn’t even his final form.
[b]Over in questland[/b], we’ve tuned up the “Find the Scholar” mission. Now only one of you needs the quest to summon Kellen, so the rest of your crew can stop pacing in circles. Also, Kellen’s Pyramid got its stairs sorted out. Fewer stumbles, more triumph. All three waves of lizardmen now show up to the fight too, because a two-wave ambush is just half-baked.
And for those just starting their journey into the darkness, fear not. [b]Tutorial UI hints[/b] are now scattered throughout the demo, dropping knowledge like enchanted scrolls of wisdom. They won’t hold your hand, but they might give you a gentle push in the right direction.

So yeah. This patch is smoother, smarter, and way more playable. Get in there, crush some monsters, sell your junk, and defend the relic like the hero you were born to be. Stay sharp, stay loud, and never stop looking cool while you save the world.
-Mechmonkey Devs

notes.title: Patch notes v 0.2.10
notes.content:
[h1]Medieval Darkness Patch V0.2.10 – Bodacious Update, Dudes![/h1]

Whoa! Listen up, portal-traveling adventurers! The Creator just dropped a most triumphant update. So grab your lutes, sharpen your swords, and get ready to rock the darkness like it’s 1989.

[b]UI Improvements – Righteous Navigation![/b]
The compass just got a little more excellent! You’ll now see a totally helpful “Go to Task” icon up top to keep you on the righteous path.

Icons for home base (aka the relic zone) have been resized for maximum clarity. You’ll never get lost in time... or town.


[b]Building – Craft On, Dudes![/b]
Stonecutters rejoice! You can now build the Stonecutter bench and start chipping away like true medieval artisans. Party on with precision!


[b]Quests – Most Triumphant Fixes![/b]
Quest objects now tell you their names, so you’re not like, “What even is this?” anymore.

Thora’s buildable campfire quest? Fixed, lit, and ready to roast mallows. You can actually complete it now. Whoa.


[b]NPC’s On the Move![/b]
Busy guys and gals like the Mayor should actually stop now when you talk to them!
[b]
Animations – Excellent Emotes![/b]
A new Taunt animation has entered the timeline. Now you can look your enemies in the eyes and say, “Bring it on, bogus beasts.”

[b]Naughtwood Defense Area – Heavy Metal Upgrades![/b]
The starting towns just got way more productive. You’ll now find new workbenches: the StoneCutter and Woodworker Bench. Craft like the wild stallions you are.


Catch you in the next patch, Strange ones!

notes.title: Patch notes v 0.2.8-Demo
notes.content:
[b]Whoa! What’s up, Strange Ones?![/b]
It’s been a few totally bogus months of silence, but don’t worry, we weren’t just chillin’ with old dudes. We’ve been hardcore rebuilding the game from the ground up, and now the demo is almost ready to rock!
We know it’s been a while, but we hope this latest update is totally worth the wait!
Super important, though: If you’ve got any old characters lying around, delete those dudes! Seriously. Keeping them around could crush your load time vibes. Start fresh with a brand new righteous hero and ride into glory.
This version is practically a whole new game, rebuilt, refined, and ready to shred. We’re way stoked for you to check it out… Thanks for hanging with us on this most excellent journey!!



[b] Patch Notes – v0.2.8 Demo! [/b]
Strange Ones, unite! We've been slammin’ code like it's a guitar solo from the heavens, and this update is packed with righteous new stuff. Read on and prepare to be most impressed.

[b] AI – Party On, NPCs![/b]
We totally rewired the brains of our NPCs using a slick new AI system. It's way more excellent now and, like, way easier for us to tweak.
Your NPC buddies now swap weapons like pros and use skills, buffs, debuffs, and heals like they’ve actually read their class manuals.
Yeah, some of them still act a little bogus—simple minds and all—but now it's way easier for us to fix their funk.
Also, say hello to rats (gnarly) and Lizardmen (double gnarly).

[b] Followers & Mercenaries – Because Soloing is for Squares[/b]
You can now recruit your very own combat bro (or sis)! These radical followers will help you rock the battlefield.
They’ll hang with you for the whole match but we’re totally talking about letting them save with your character later.
We’ve got tiers of followers, each one gnarlier than the last, with more skills and better stats than your mom’s meatloaf.
Wanna change their gear? Do it! Their combat vibes shift based on what you slap on them.
Oh! And they can now run the forge and smelter while you’re off slaying demons or jamming in town. Early days, but soon they’ll be doing your whole to-do list while you chill.

 [b]Performance – Faster Than Rufus’s Time Machine[/b]
We tuned the game’s engine like a vintage Les Paul.
Players on lower-end rigs are seeing 50-100% better framerates. That's not a typo—it's a time warp.
Higher-end PCs are getting smoother vibes too, just not as dramatic. Either way: Everything just feels better, man.

[b] Proximity Traps – Watch Your Step, Dude[/b]
Added three new traps that trigger when you get too close. Totally not sketchy.
Area Trap: Spike pits, fire pits, and other gnarly surprises.
Missile Trap: Boom! It shoots stuff. You’ll see.
Moving Trap: May not hurt, but might toss you into a pit. Or a gig. Who knows?

[b]New Zone:Naughtwood Area – Welcome to the Jungle!![/b]
Venture into a tropical paradise filled with ancient Lizardmen temples and sweaty danger. It’s like vacation, but with more death.

[b] Misc – Odds, Ends, and Face-Melters[/b]
Brand new theme song added. Huge shout-out to Nick for laying down the track. It slaps!
We totally reworked the starting area based on your feedback. It’s more enclosed, way more linear, and now has some actual lore baked in.
Quests now support object activation. Push stuff! Touch glowing things! You get the idea.
And yeah… a whole bunch of bug fixes. Like, a bug swarm’s worth.

[b]Known Bugs – These Dudes Still Party Too Hard[/b]
Some NPCs get stuck during pathing like they’re on an existential quest. Especially near the Relic in Naughtwood—they just love that thing.
Some events may not spawn all their waves, so they can’t be finished. Super bogus, and we’re on it.
Stay wild. Stay strange. And most importantly...
Be excellent to each other. 🤘
 [i]— The Dev Dudes from Mech Monkey Studios[/i]

notes.title: patch notes: 8-20-24
notes.content:
This is a minor update in preperation for a larger update with AI and soon to be released NPC followers. Soon you will be able to hire an npc to go into battle with you!

[b]General changes/bug fixes[/b]

Ui changes on the the training window.
Ladders updated, animations now play when you use them.


[b]Items:[/b]
Vetterland armor line added
Wolf armor 

[b]Spell changes:[/b]

[b]Zealot[/b]
Added new spells: Blood Sacrifice and Holy Word.
Blood Sacrifice is an ae heal that costs health and heals all targets around the caster.
Holy word is a buff that imbues the recipient with extra holy damage.
Reduced the healing recovery of Creator's Blessing
Zealot's now have access to the Righteous Destruction spell

[b]Mage:[/b]
Reduced the level requirements for Fireball and haste

[b]Quests:[/b]

Camp guard now has the wolf armor quest line.

notes.title: update notes 7-19-24
notes.content:
Large visual changes!
Terrain textures were upgraded and tweaked for the town of Naughtwood and the Magical Forest.
Vegetation changed for both Naughtwood and Magical Forest. These changes include much more underbrush that helps provide cover for creatures. Be careful out there!

Sound upgrade!
A total overhaul of the way sounds and music work in game! Combat music plays when players are attacked.
Added voice packs to new characters and monsters. 
Please create new characters to get your voice heard!

Emotes!
Players can now do emotes by using slash commands. The current ones in the game are:
/emote dance1
/emote chickendance
/emote zealot
/emote mage


Other
More creatures were added to the new animation system.
Other players can be revived for a short time after being downed. Zealot's Resurrect spell gives XP back to the player.
Players can now trade items between themselves.

Known issues:
Swapping inventory items on NPC's may have unintended consequences.
Combat music doesn't always stop after combat is over.
Issues with emote music, it doesn't always play or plays for a very short time.
